questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to invest your money wisely in property
Why poor countries are getting richer every year
The history of sailing and famous boat races
The super rich and why they love expensive yachts
questions.why: Catherine says they're looking into the lives of the super rich and one of their favourite pastimes: yachts.

questions.q: How much is the number of super rich people expected to grow over the next ten years?
options: By 30%
By 43%
By 62%
questions.why: Neil says the number of super rich is expected to increase by 43% over the next decade.

questions.q: What did a report last year say about the world's richest 62 people?
options: They owned as much as the poorest half of the world
They all owned superyachts that were over 100 metres
Their wealth was falling for the first time in years
Most of them lived in Vietnam or other parts of Asia
questions.why: Catherine says the 62 richest individuals owned as much as the poorest 50% of people in the world.

questions.q: What did the academic's research find the super rich spend money on?
options: Art and wine
Private islands
Yachts
Football clubs
questions.why: Neil answers 'Yachts!', calling them the ultimate status symbol.

questions.q: Why does Emma Spence mention private jets, wine and art?
options: They keep or grow their value, unlike yachts
They are more expensive than yachts
They are the most popular status symbols
The super rich no longer buy them
questions.why: She says these are investable assets that make good business sense, 'whereas a superyacht is essentially a black hole'.

questions.q: What does Emma Spence mean by calling a superyacht a 'black hole'?
options: It is painted black
It is very hard to find
It is dangerous to sail
It swallows money and loses value
questions.why: Neil says superyachts actually lose money, and in business terms a black hole eats all your money.

questions.q: How did Emma Spence start studying superyachts?
options: She owned one herself
She used to work on them
Her family built them
She wrote about them for a newspaper
questions.why: Catherine says that's how Emma began her study: she used to work on the yachts.

questions.q: What does the size of your yacht show, according to Emma's research?
options: How fast you can travel between different countries
How many crew members you can afford to pay each year
Your social position, which decides your place in the harbour
How many years you and your family have been wealthy
questions.why: Neil says yacht size shows your place in the pecking order, and higher up gets the best place in the harbour.
